question: Assume today is 2026-08-29. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total freight carried by Canadian railways in July 2026, in tonnes, as it will be first reported by Statistics Canada in its monthly Railway carloadings release (total traffic carried, Canada).

target.what: Total freight carried by Canadian railways (all traffic carried, Canada) during July 2026, as first reported by Statistics Canada in its monthly Railway carloadings release (Table 23-10-0219-01 / The Daily release 'Railway carloadings, monthly'). Counts all revenue freight loaded and carried by Cana
target.caveats: Working interpretation: the headline 'total traffic carried' tonnage (all commodities, all traffic including domestic, transborder and international) for the calendar month of July 2026, as first published (not revised). Alternative interpretations that would change the number: (a) 'freight carried'

candidates.perspective: Statistics Canada monthly Railway carloadings time series
candidates.hypothesis: July 2026 total traffic carried will be close to the same month in prior years adjusted for trend and any 2026-specific shocks; July is a seasonal peak month for grain and potash. The historical July values and recent monthly values (through the last release before the cutoff, likely June 2026) anchor the level and seasonality.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly total traffic carried (all commodities, tonnes) for Canada from Table 23-10-0219-01 for July 2023, July 2024, July 2025, plus the most recent months published before 2026-08-29 (e.g., Jan-Jun 2026 and full-year 2025). Minimum: July values for 3-5 prior years and the latest 3-6 monthly prints.
search_hints: Statistics Canada table 23-10-0219-01 railway carloadings total traffic carried tonnes

candidates.hypothesis: Total tonnes = sum over commodity groups (grain, potash, coal, chemicals, forest products, metals, intermodal, etc.) of tonnes carried. Commodity-level July history plus known 2026 supply signals (grain harvest/carryover, potash output, coal exports) constrain the total and its largest swing components.

methods.label: m1

p38.role: total freight moved by rail in Canada, full year 2025 (annual level base)

a2.role: July seasonal factor relative to annual monthly average

methods.rationale: Annual 2025 total (376.6 Mt) divided by 12 gives the monthly average; multiply by a July seasonal factor near 1.0 (July 2025 was 30.7 Mt vs 31.4 Mt monthly average). Captures the level and seasonality but not the 2026 change; a2 carries that uncertainty.

methods.label: m2

p73.role: total cargo carried by Canadian railways, all traffic, Canada, July 2025

methods.rationale: Direct year-over-year scaling of the July 2025 StatCan total (30.7 Mt) by the RAC-implied 2026 change factor. Same month, same definition, one year gap; the change factor is anchored on RAC YTD carloads/RTMs and grain growth. Strongest route because it uses the exact target definition and period.

methods.label: m3

p3.role: monthly average total traffic carried, 1999-2020 (long-run level base)

a2.role: July seasonal factor relative to annual monthly average

methods.rationale: Long-run monthly average (26.4 Mt, 1999-2020) times July seasonal factor. Older vintage and lower level than 2025, so it serves as a conservative lower-bound cross-check rather than a primary estimate; included to widen the combination's robustness.

kept.name: July 2026 total traffic vs July 2025 change factor
kept.rationale: RAC 2026 YTD shows carloads flat and RTMs +4% (p61), with grain & fertilizers +11% carloads / +13% RTMs (p64-p67) and grain crop-year +15% (p70). Grain is a large July component, so a modest positive change is expected; metals/minerals flat (p68) and US-connection traffic weak in 2025 (p42, p76) tem
kept.applies_when: July 2026 tonnage tracks the RAC YTD direction and no major disruption hits July 2026.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of a July 2026 labour disruption, wildfire, or tariff shock cutting volumes, or RAC data showing a sharp July decline.

kept.name: July seasonal factor relative to annual monthly average
kept.rationale: July 2025 (30.7 Mt, p73) is close to the 2025 monthly average (376.6/12 = 31.4 Mt, p38) and slightly above the five-year July average (29.8 Mt, p75). July is a moderate-to-strong month but not a sharp peak; factor near 1.0 with modest spread.
kept.applies_when: The 2026 annual level is similar to 2025 and July is a near-average month.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that July 2026 is a strong grain peak far above the annual average, or a collapse below it.
